chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

The woman in istihadah refrains for the days of her menstrual period, then she takes precaution by one or two days. If she sees purity, she performs ghusl; and if she does not see purity, she performs ghusl and inserts cotton. She continues to perform salat with that ghusl until blood appears upon the cotton; then, when the blood appears, she repeats the ghusl and replaces the cotton.

key_terms.احْتَشَتْ: she inserted cotton to contain or check the blood
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفِ: the cotton used to monitor the bleeding
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istihadah, irregular uterine bleeding outside normal menstruation
key_terms.طُهْرًا: a state of purity from bleeding
key_terms.قُرْئِهَا: her menstrual period or known cycle days

ai.seo_question: What should a woman in istihadah do regarding ghusl, precautionary waiting, and salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the mustahadah regarding how long she refrains based on her known menstrual days and an added precaution of one or two days. It then explains her ghusl, use of cotton, and continuation of salat until the blood reaches the cotton, at which point she renews the ghusl and the cotton.
